R591.note: Regex allowlist on reportName correctly blocks all batch/cmd metacharacters since Process.Start of a .bat falls back to cmd.exe parsing, but the new allowlist rejects any previously-accepted report name outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] (spaces, dots, etc.) that the original code and no stated contract restricted.

R592.note: SLF4J {} parameterized logging avoids format-string style issues but does not strip CR/LF from the substituted value, so log-forging via embedded newlines is not actually neutralized; contract (ERROR+exception on failure, 401/200, INFO on success) is otherwise preserved exactly.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID filename is an appropriate CWE-434 fix and matches the stated 200/400 contract shape, but the allowlist rejects any file type outside the 7 listed extensions that the original code and stated contract did not restrict.

R594.note: doubleCsrfProtection double-submit middleware is a reasonable synchronizer-token mechanism, but no route in the case (or the write-up) issues the CSRF cookie/token to the client, so every legitimate authenticated transfer would now fail even though the contract requires them to still succeed - not disclosed.

R595.note: Magic-byte signature validation plus server-generated filename is a strong CWE-434 fix, but it rejects any legitimate file type outside the 4 signatures checked (pdf/png/jpg/gif) that the original code and stated contract did not restrict.

R596.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CSRF middleware exactly as the stated contract requires (valid-token POSTs still succeed, 401/405 shapes untouched); no other observable change.

R597.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex replaces the seedable mt_rand token with a proper CSPRNG token; format change (hex string vs small integer) is disclosed and doesn't reject any legitimate caller since only DB storage/email consume it.

R598.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to HmacSha256 matches the symmetric signing key already in use, closing algorithm-confusion without affecting legitimately-issued HS256 tokens.

R599.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus Path.startsWith containment correctly closes Zip Slip, but the added single-filename-only check rejects every entry containing a path separator, which silently breaks the stated contract requirement that valid nested archive entries still extract - not disclosed.

R600.note: Removes the erroneous second decode and replaces the weak contains("..") check with getCanonicalPath containment validation; files are stored flat so legitimate flat filenames are unaffected.

R601.note: The Unix branch (ls -- data via exec(String[])) correctly closes both shell-metachar and flag injection, but the Windows branch still execs cmd.exe /c with dir/data as array elements - cmd.exe re-parses its own /c command line for &,|,etc. regardless of argv separation, so Windows metacharacter injection is not actually closed.

R602.note: Standard database/sql parameterized query with ? placeholder; output, Scan, and error handling unchanged.

R603.note: Detailed error logged server-side, generic message sent to client - the message-content change is the intended fix itself and is fully disclosed; status code and control flow unchanged.

R604.note: .RequireAuthorization() on the Minimal API DELETE endpoint restores parity with the sibling [Authorize]-protected controller; no broader restriction added.

R605.note: Switching to Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API is the right general approach and CRLF rejection is a reasonable defense-in-depth, but the fix never calls store.connect() before folder.open(), so as written every legitimate call would throw IllegalStateException at runtime - not disclosed; also silently changes the method signature from Socket to Session with no caller shown.

R606.note: Switching to plain CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler correctly fixes the documented Xor-handler/raw-cookie mismatch, but forcing HttpOnly=true (dropping withHttpOnlyFalse()) removes the only way the case's SPA architecture (per its own docstring) can read the token via JavaScript, and no header/endpoint is actually added to compensate - silently breaks the described legitimate flow.
